newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge sees boost from Zambia copper.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge sees boost from Zambia copper.

text.p: Falconbridge Ltd says its participation in a consortium to mine copper in Zambia could boost the company's copper production by about 30 percent.

Falconbridge announced this week that the consortium had signed a deal to conduct a feasibility study on the Konkola Deep copper project and eventually buy a majority share in a new company that will include the copper site.
"This project meets all the criteria for a world class copper project," Falconbridge chief financial officer Lars-Eric Johansson said in an interview on Wednesday.
Falconbridge has a 30 percent stake in the consortium.

The other partners are Zambia Copper Investments Ltd -- an associate of Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd -- and Gencor Ltd. The consortium signed a memorandum of understanding with Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd on Tuesday.
Falconbridge's 30 percent stake in the consortium will likely translate into copper production of 50,000 tonnes a year if the mine is developed, Johansson said.
Falconbridge will also be responsible for 30 percent of the estimated US$700 million to US$800 million it will cost to develop the project, he said.

The copper would boost Falconbridge's total copper production by 30 percent from today's levels, he said. But once the company's Collahuasi copper project in Chile comes on stream in 1998, the Zambian copper will mean a rise of 15 percent in total copper production.
While Zambia has long been recognized as a major copper producer, the Zambian government has only recently allowed foreign corporations to participate in the mining sector.
The Konkola Deep project contains a resource of 340 million tonnes at 3.8 percent copper and should sustain mining for more than 30 years, the consortium said in a statement.
